post.title: How Shraddha Aarogya Mandir Digitised 25 Years of Medical Records with Healthray
post.excerpt: Shraddha Aarogya Mandir has looked after Vapi for more than 25 years. It is a 150-bed multispeciality hospital, with cardiology, orthopaedics, surgery, gynaecology and intensive care all in one building. A hospital that old keeps a lot of paper. That paper is where the day kept getting stuck.

fields.hero_lede: Shraddha Aarogya Mandir has looked after Vapi for more than 25 years. It is a 150-bed multispeciality hospital, with cardiology, orthopaedics, surgery, gynaecology and intensive care all in one building. A hospital that old keeps a lot of paper. That paper is where the day kept getting stuck.

glance_facts.label: Location
glance_facts.value: Opposite Sanidhya Apartment, Ganeshwadi, Shanthi Nagar, Vapi, Gujarat

overview_content: For years, every patient visit meant another sheet in a folder. The folders filled cabinets, and someone had to walk over and pull the right one by hand each time a doctor asked.

That worked when the hospital was smaller. At 150 beds and 12 departments, it stopped working. The file a doctor needed was often upstairs, or in use somewhere else, and the whole visit sat there waiting for it.
fields.problem_intro: Nothing here was dramatic. These were four small delays that happened over and over, every day.

problems.title: Records Out of Reach
problems.text: Pulling a paper file took minutes, and now and then it just could not be found. So a doctor either stood waiting, or re-ran a test whose result was already sitting in that same folder.

problems.title: Billing Left for the End
problems.text: At discharge, someone added up the charges by hand off a pile of slips. The patient was ready to go home and still had to wait at the counter while that total got built.

problems.title: Pharmacy Running Blind
problems.text: Stock and dispensing sat in different registers. A medicine could run low and nobody knew until it was gone, and what went out did not always line up with what the bill said.

problems.title: Numbers No One Could See
problems.text: Occupancy and revenue were kept in registers. Ask how last week went and you waited days, because someone had to count it all up first.

fields.decision_intro: A consultant on how the record changed her clinic.
fields.quote_text: A patient would be sitting in front of me while someone went off to find her old file. Sometimes it never showed up. Now I type her name and the whole history is right there, so I can look at her first instead of waiting on paper.
fields.solution_intro: Healthray took those same four jams and moved them onto one system the whole hospital works from.

solutions.title: The Record Opens Instantly
solutions.text: Notes, tests and prescriptions all live in one file. A doctor pulls it up at the bedside. Nothing gets fetched, and nothing gets ordered a second time.

solutions.title: The Bill Builds Itself
solutions.text: Each charge posts the moment care is given. By the time the patient reaches the counter, the total is already done.

solutions.title: Pharmacy on the Same System
solutions.text: Dispensing comes off live stock and goes straight onto the bill. Low stock shows up early, and nothing leaves the shelf unaccounted.

solutions.title: The Week on One Screen
solutions.text: Occupancy, revenue, department load — all of it updates as it happens. A manager can read today's numbers today.

fields.setup_intro: Healthray did it in three stages, and the wards never once went down.

steps.title: Shadowed the Floor
steps.text: Healthray spent a week sitting with each department, watching how its files, tests and charges really move.

steps.title: Carried the Archive
steps.text: Twenty-five years of records were digitised and loaded, so no patient turned up to a blank screen.

steps.title: Walked Beside Staff
steps.text: Support stayed on the floor through the first live weeks, sorting out questions right at the desk.

fields.results_intro: Measured and estimated across the first months on the system.

results.title: Files Pulled in Seconds
results.text: What used to take a runner a few minutes now opens on the ward in one tap. Rounds keep moving from one patient to the next with no gap in between.

results.title: Pharmacy That Reconciles
results.text: What gets dispensed now matches the bill, line for line. And low stock shows its hand before the shelf is empty, not after a patient has been sent away.

results.title: Discharge Without the Counter Wait
results.text: The charges are already in, so the discharge bill closes in minutes. The bed opens up and the family gets to leave at the same time.

results.title: A Week You Can Actually Read
results.text: The dashboards do the counting now. Management can see occupancy, revenue and load whenever they want it, instead of waiting days for a tally.
